findings.section: all phase headings vs in-body references

findings.criterion: 3 — The latch cannot be burned hermetically
findings.section: Phase 2 (CLOSED provenance vocabulary) vs Phase 1 repair path
findings.message: The frozen `usage_state` vocabulary excludes `sidecar-root-unavailable` — yet that state demonstrably exists on disk (3 intake records), the Phase-1 repair script's precondition check must RECOGNIZE it ("verify the current state is still `sidecar-root-unavailable`"), and, worse, the plan never defines what a BEACONED finalize emits when the sidecar root or the session's sidecar file is missing at finalize time — the exact failure mode that caused the intake poisoning. Does it defer? Emit `unmeasured`? Consume the claim? The conformance test asserting "no writer ever emits a value outside these sets" will either fail against reality or force an ad-hoc, untested state back in — vocabulary drift by emergency, the precise accretion the freeze exists to prevent. Name the sidecar-missing-under-beacon outcome explicitly (it should be non-CAS-consuming and retryable), and state whether legacy out-of-vocabulary states are reader-tolerated or migrated.

findings.criterion: 3 — The latch cannot be burned hermetically
findings.section: Phase 1 (hermetic beacon, CAS trust model)
findings.message: The plan claims to "invert the hermetic predicate from blocklist to positive identity," but the beacon mint condition is "exclusive bind on 8777 + the REAL un-redirected data dir" — and determining "un-redirected" is itself a blocklist check over redirect seams (is `ANCHOR_DATA_DIR` set?). The foresight brief names a SECOND seam the beacon predicate never consults: `ANCHOR_SIDECAR_DIR`, "the only hermetic escape." A manual-debug run on 8777 with the real data dir but a redirected sidecar root mints a valid beacon, is admitted to the CAS, reads the wrong (empty) sidecar root, and consumes the claim — recreating the poison class criterion 3 exists to kill, through the front door of the trust model. Either the beacon mint must refuse when ANY redirect seam is active (and the plan must maintain that seam list as new seams are added — say so, so a future maintainer adding a seam knows to touch the beacon), or a beaconed finalize that cannot locate the sidecar must be non-CAS-consuming per Finding 3. The "no supervisor enumeration to get wrong" boast is overstated; it traded supervisor enumeration for seam enumeration and didn't write the seam list down.

findings.criterion: 1 — Swarm spend visible going forward
findings.section: Phase 3 (launch-surface table tier 5, deferred items) vs Phase 1 trust model
findings.message: Stage-0 decision 4 locks "BOTH eager owner finalize + reconcile-dead catch-all." But under the Phase-1 trust model, only the beaconed server process may consume the CAS — and the agy-dispatch orchestrator is a separate CLI process that can never hold the beacon. The plan's own deferred item ("eager IN-PROCESS finalize inside the agy-dispatch skill itself") is therefore structurally impossible as named: a future maintainer who picks up that deferred task will build it, watch the beacon refuse admission on every call, and have to invent an unplanned workaround (a service finalize endpoint? beacon delegation?) at the highest-risk primitive. For the entire skill-layer swarm — 106 of 111 registry sessions, the population criterion 1 exists for — "eager owner finalize" quietly degrades to "sweep-only, up to ~30 minutes late," which is fine but is a MATERIAL narrowing of a locked decision that the plan should state honestly rather than defer as if it were buildable. Either specify the mechanism (e.g. the orchestrator POSTs a finalize request to the beaconed service, which performs the admitted write) or amend the deferred item to say sweep-is-the-owner for skill-layer sessions, permanently.

findings.criterion: 3 — a later live finalize can still measure (and 6, honest counting)
findings.section: Phase 1 (deferred stamping) + Phase 3 (widened sweep)
findings.message: `finalize-deferred` is retryable forever: the ~30-minute sweep "RETR[ies] every finalize-deferred record" with no exit condition, and the healthcheck WARNs "when live-registry sessions accumulate deferrals." A session whose sidecar never existed (or was pruned pre-capture) will defer on every sweep until the end of time — the deferred count only grows, and the yellow WARN becomes permanent wallpaper. The plan itself pins the locked severity rule's rationale: "a false alarm just trains the eye to ignore the banner." A permanently-yellow WARN is the same hazard one tier down. The vocabulary contains `unmeasured` but no transition rule deferred→unmeasured is defined anywhere — a future maintainer inherits an unbounded retry queue with no policy for declaring a session honestly unmeasurable. Define the terminality rule (e.g. N sweeps or sidecar-provably-absent ⇒ `unmeasured`, terminal, non-CAS-consuming... or explicitly "deferred is forever, WARN only above a delta threshold") — either is defensible; silence is not.

findings.criterion: 1 — Swarm spend visible going forward
findings.section: Phase 3 (forward orphan-sidecar sweep)
findings.message: The sweep's stated trigger is "sidecars whose DIRNAME embeds a valid session marker but has no registry row" — but the dirname is keyed to a CWD, and the sweep's explicit target population (tier-b skill-layer spawns that bypass the wrapper, i.e. a skill invoking raw `claude` from inside a parent session's worktree) produces exactly the collision case: MULTIPLE session JSONL files inside ONE dirname that embeds the PARENT's session id. Does the sweep mint one record per dir (silently summing sub-agents into the parent)? One per JSONL file (against what session id — they have engine UUIDs, no registry rows)? Skip as ambiguous (silently dropping the very spend the tier-b catch-all promises to catch)? The plan specifies dirname↔id correlation for the ONE-file-per-dir case and says nothing about N-files-per-dir, which is the dominant bypass shape. Specify the attribution rule (parent-attribution with a `via-parent-worktree` provenance note would be honest) — otherwise "never invisible" is asserted, not designed.

findings.criterion: 3 — The latch cannot be burned hermetically
findings.section: Phase 2 (quiesce check)
findings.message: "Truncated tail → `usage_state: measured-partial`, never a clean-looking number" — but does writing a measured-partial record CONSUME the exclusive-create claim? If yes, a transiently-truncated sidecar (AV lock, partial flush that the N-second mtime window happened to miss) permanently latches an undercount that append-only forbids ever correcting — a burned-latch variant in miniature. If no, what stops every subsequent sweep from re-reading and re-emitting? The claim-file semantics are defined for measured/deferred but not for partial. One sentence fixes it (e.g. partial consumes the claim ONLY after quiesce confirms the file can no longer grow — process provably dead — else defer).

findings.criterion: 4 — History recovered, honestly labeled
findings.section: Phase 0 (plan-time sidecar snapshot)
findings.message: "Mark the archive read-only (attrib +R / ACL)" — on Windows, `attrib +R` on a DIRECTORY does not prevent creation, modification, or deletion of files within it; it is cosmetically meaningless for the stated goal. Only a deny-write ACL actually freezes the archive, and the plan offers the two as interchangeable ("attrib +R / ACL"). A future maintainer will take the cheap option and believe the snapshot is immutable when it isn't — undermining the "frozen snapshot" premise every backfill guarantee is anchored to. Also, "the disk cost is bounded" is asserted with no number: 55+ dirs of full JSONL transcripts for multi-million-token sessions plausibly runs to gigabytes; state the measured size before committing to copy-everything, or the Phase-0 operator discovers it mid-copy. Specify: deny-write ACL (not attrib), and record the actual byte total in the plan once measured.

findings.criterion: 1 — Swarm spend visible going forward ("A new fleet run produces measured records for its sub-agent sessions")
findings.section: Phase 4 — tier (b) sweep catch-all / forward orphan-sidecar sweep
findings.message: Steel-manning the premise: the plan's guarantee for the DOMINANT population (106 of 111 registry sessions are swarm) is "measured eagerly where wrapped, by sweep otherwise — never silently absent." The sweep's predicate is "sidecars whose dirname embeds a valid session marker but has no registry row." But a skill-layer sub-agent spawned WITHOUT the wrapper (the exact bypass tier (b) exists for) typically inherits the parent session's cwd — so its sidecar lands under the SAME munged project dirname as the parent. That dirname embeds the PARENT's session id, which DOES have a registry row, so the orphan predicate structurally never fires; the sub-agent's spend is either silently folded into (or mis-attributed against) the parent, or never minted at all. The "never invisible" claim is therefore false for precisely the population criterion 1 exists for, and the enforcement backstop (a grep conformance test over Anchor product code) cannot reach the actual spawner either — agy-dispatch is a skill in a different repo whose runtime `claude` invocations are model-driven prompts, not greppable Anchor call sites. The plan must either (a) require per-spawn distinct cwd/worktree so the dirname correlation holds per sub-agent, (b) correlate at sidecar-FILE granularity (per-file session UUID) rather than per-dir, or (c) honestly demote the tier-(b) guarantee from "never invisible" to "invisible unless wrapped" and make wrapper adoption a gating deliverable, not a named task.

findings.criterion: 3 — The latch cannot be burned hermetically
findings.section: Phase 2 — CAS trust model, writers 2 and 5
findings.message: Writer 5 declares the invariant "No measurement without a beacon, ever." Writer 2 (the backfill tool) holds no beacon — it runs precisely when the service is UNREACHABLE — yet mints `measured-backfill` records through "the identical claim path." Both statements cannot be true. As written, either the invariant is false (and the trust model's headline guarantee is rhetorical, not real), or backfill needs a beacon it structurally cannot have. The fix is a restatement, not a redesign — the true invariant is "no CAS consumption except by the current beacon holder OR the audited standalone operator CLI under its own admission predicate" — but a trust model whose single authoritative table contains a self-contradiction has not earned the word "authoritative," and the STUB-GATE tests pinning criterion 3 will pin whichever reading the implementer happens to choose.

findings.criterion: 4 — History recovered, honestly labeled
findings.section: Phase 2 repair path / Phase 4 sweep scope / Phase 7 target set
findings.message: Phase 4 names the beaconed sweep "the single named owner of deferred retries," retrying every `finalize-deferred` record against the LIVE sidecar root on a ~30-minute cadence from the interim deploy checkpoint onward. Phase 2's repair path re-stamps the 3 poisoned records `finalize-deferred` and then asserts "the Phase 6 backfill measures them through the normal claim path." Both cannot own them: the sweep will reach those records phases earlier than backfill, reading the live root (which engine retention may have pruned differently than the Phase-0 snapshot), and whichever writer wins the exclusive-create claim forecloses the other. Consequences the plan does not resolve: (a) the repaired sessions may be stamped `measured` (sweep) rather than `measured-backfill` (backfill), so the Phase 7 outcome list's target set ("69 + 37 + 3 repaired-deferred") will not reconcile as written; (b) if the live sidecar was pruned but the snapshot copy survives, the sweep's retry fails first and the plan does not state whether a failed live retry leaves the record retryable for backfill or stamps a terminal-looking state. Name ONE owner per record class (e.g. sweep owns post-deploy deferrals; backfill exclusively owns pre-snapshot historical sessions, sweep skips them) or the "single named owner" claim is decorative.

findings.criterion: 2 — `__doctor__` is excluded from every surface
findings.section: Phase 6 — synthetic-session predicate
findings.message: The convention test "registering synthetic without the flag fails loudly" is unenforceable as specified: to detect that an unflagged registration is synthetic, the test must identify syntheticness by some signal other than the flag — which is name-sniffing, the exact mechanism the plan bans ("marker convention, never name-sniffing"). Either the test quietly reintroduces name-sniffing (acceptable ONLY inside the test as a tripwire, which the plan should say explicitly), or the guarantee degrades to "callers that remember the flag are excluded," which is a convention, not an enforcement — and per the project's own engine-vs-convention honesty table, it should be labeled as such. Also unstated: the migration step for EXISTING `__doctor__` registry rows that predate the flag; without it, criterion 2's "excluded from every surface" fails on day one for historical doctor sessions.

findings.criterion: 4 — History recovered, honestly labeled
findings.section: Phase ordering rationale / Phase 7
findings.message: Steel-manning the ordering premise: "backfill LAST because the substrate must soak" was compelling when delay risked data loss — but Phase 0's plan-time frozen snapshot removes that risk entirely, and the claim path backfill reuses is soaked by every earlier phase regardless of when backfill's CORRELATION logic first runs. The intake motivation (106 unmeasured swarm sessions) is the single most user-visible deliverable, and it now lands in the second-to-last phase with zero earlier evidence that the correlation will actually recover a useful fraction. A read-only backfill DRY-RUN (correlate against the snapshot, print the recovered/no-sidecar/ambiguous-skipped outcome list, mint NOTHING) belongs in Phase 3 alongside the munging-function tests: it consumes no CAS, touches no record, and converts "we believe 55+ dirs correlate" from intake-time hope into measured plan-time fact — or reveals in week one that the recovery rate is poor while there is still budget to react.

findings.criterion: 4 — History recovered, honestly labeled
findings.section: Phase 1 (Phase 0 — plan-time sidecar snapshot)
findings.message: The snapshot copies "the ENTIRE engine sidecar root — every sidecar project dir, unfiltered" into `.anchor/sidecar-archive/` — that is a byte-for-byte copy of every Claude conversation transcript on the machine, for every project (not just Anchor's), including whatever proprietary/commercial content those sessions touched. It is placed INSIDE the git working tree of a repo that already tracks and commits `.anchor/**` state files, and the sole confidentiality control is one conditional line: "add it to `.gitignore` if not already excluded." A read-only ACL does not stop `git add -A`; a single missed gitignore turns the most sensitive data concentration on the host into a committed — and, given this repo's remote-push machinery, pushable — artifact. The over-inclusive-copy rationale (munging rule untested) does not require in-tree placement: the phase's own verification step already greps for the `…anchor-worktrees-<session_id>` marker, so the same marker could bound the copy, and in any case the archive can live OUTSIDE the repo tree (e.g. `%LOCALAPPDATA%\anchor\sidecar-archive` or a sibling dir) with its path recorded in the manifest. Require: archive location outside the working tree, OR marker-filtered copy plus a manifest listing of excluded dirs — plus a test asserting the archive path is never under the repo root.

findings.criterion: 3 — The latch cannot be burned hermetically
findings.section: Phase 2 — hermetic beacon substrate / CAS trust model row 1
findings.message: The plan specifies how the beacon is MINTED (exclusive 8777 bind + real data dir at startup) but never how it is PRESENTED at consume time. The residual-risk admission ("a malicious local process could copy the beacon file") reveals the implied design: the beacon is a FILE in the real data dir, and "presenting the matching beacon" means matching that file's content. That check is circular: any process that resolves the real data dir can read the beacon file and present it — and "hermetic context accidentally resolving the real data dir" is the EXACT bug class that caused the original poisoning (the healthcheck was not a telemetry test, so the Phase-2 telemetry-suite conformance test would not have caught it). As written, the positive-identity predicate degrades to "can read a file," which is anti-nothing. The fix is cheap and must be pinned: consume-time verification must be self-identity, not file-content matching — the finalizing code compares its OWN process identity (PID + in-memory boot token) against the minted beacon, i.e. finalize-with-consume is legal only in-process inside the beacon-holding server; out-of-process callers are structurally deferred. Add a named STUB-GATE: a process that can read the beacon file but is not the minting PID gets `finalize-deferred`, CAS intact.

findings.criterion: 4 — never overwrites a live-measured record; honest provenance
findings.section: Phase 2 CAS design / Phase 4 sweep / Phase 7 backfill
findings.message: The CAS convergence argument rests on "record content is idempotent (same session → same payload) so a double-fire converges." That holds only WITHIN a writer class. Across classes it is false: the Phase-4 sweep retries every `finalize-deferred` record against the LIVE sidecar root and mints `measured`, while the Phase-7 backfill targets the SAME historical population (69 no-usage-state + 37 uncorrelated + 3 repaired-deferred) against the FROZEN snapshot and mints `measured-backfill` — different provenance, and potentially different token totals wherever the live sidecar grew or was pruned after the plan-time snapshot. The interim deploy checkpoint at the end of Phase 4 guarantees this overlap window exists for weeks before backfill runs. Exactly one writer wins the exclusive-create, arbitrarily — so a given historical session's provenance AND numbers become race-dependent and non-reproducible, which is precisely the dishonesty class this effort exists to eliminate. The plan's race test pins only sweep-vs-eager (same payload); the sweep-vs-backfill pairing — the one with divergent payloads — is untested and unacknowledged. Require an explicit precedence rule (e.g. sweep/live-root measurement wins for any session whose live sidecar still exists; backfill claims only sessions the sweep has confirmed absent-from-live-root) plus a STUB-GATE for the divergent-payload pairing.

findings.criterion: 4 — History recovered, honestly labeled
findings.section: Phase 7 run discipline vs Phase 2 CAS trust model row 2
findings.message: Phase 2's authoritative writer table admits the backfill tool on a fixed predicate that includes "service-unreachable probe (8777)" — no override is listed, and the table is presented as THE single trust model. Phase 7 then quietly adds "REFUSES to run while the service is reachable unless `--force`". That is an internal contradiction in the plan's own security spec, and the flag it introduces defeats the one guard that prevents the backfill from racing the live service's periodic sweep on the same claim namespace (amplifying Finding 4: with `--force`, the divergent-payload race is not an unlucky window but an operator-invitable steady state). The service-reachable refusal exists precisely because concurrent operation was judged unsafe; an escape hatch with no stated justification, no logging requirement, and no mention in the trust-model table is a hole, not a convenience. Either delete `--force`, or add it to the trust-model row with its admission conditions (why, when, what it logs, what additional check replaces the probe) and a test pinning its behavior.

findings.criterion: 1 — Swarm spend visible going forward (and the Statement's "nothing is ever fabricated")
findings.section: Phase 4 — forward orphan-sidecar sweep
findings.message: The forward sweep mints honest-provenance `measured-backfill` records for any sidecar dir "whose dirname embeds a valid session marker but has no registry row." Unlike the Phase-7 backfill — which cross-checks containment against the complete KNOWN-session-id set and demands exactly one match — the forward sweep's admission is stated as dirname-marker-plus-parseable-JSONL alone, with explicitly NO registry row required. That means the trust anchor for a spend record entering real surfaces is a directory NAME: any process (or accident — a restored/copied old worktree dir, a user hand-running `claude` inside a stale worktree path, a test escaping to the real sidecar root from the non-telemetry suite the conformance test doesn't cover) that produces a marker-shaped dirname with JSONL inside gets its numbers summed into the project rollup as measured spend for a session Anchor never launched. The Statement's "nothing is ever fabricated" is violated by construction — fabrication just has to arrive as a plausible dirname. Require the forward sweep to enforce the SAME exactly-one-known-session-id containment check as backfill (the "unregistered launch" case it exists for still passes, because the choke-point helper registers before exec — a sidecar with no resolvable registry session should be REPORTED as an anomaly, never silently minted).

findings.criterion: 3 — The latch cannot be burned hermetically
findings.section: Phase 2 — hermetic predicate inversion
findings.message: The beacon predicate is exclusive-8777-bind + real DATA dir — the sidecar root is not part of the identity. Two consequent holes. (a) A process holding a legitimate beacon but running with `ANCHOR_SIDECAR_DIR` redirected (the plan's own "only hermetic escape" seam) — e.g. a dev hand-runs the server on 8777, real data dir, with a leftover sidecar redirect in the shell env — is a fully-admitted CAS consumer that will find no sidecar for any real session. That is the ORIGINAL poison scenario (`sidecar-root-unavailable` consuming the latch) re-admitted through the front door, and the plan never states what usage_state a beaconed finalize records when the sidecar is absent — `sidecar-root-unavailable` is conspicuously NOT in the closed vocabulary, and no rule maps sidecar-absence to the non-terminal `finalize-deferred`. (b) Symmetrically, a pytest run while the service is stopped (e.g. mid-warm-restart) that spawns the real server module without redirecting the data dir wins the 8777 bind and mints a valid beacon — the manual-debug carve-out makes this by-design admissible, so criterion 3's guarantee silently narrows to "while the real service happens to be running." Require: (1) `ANCHOR_SIDECAR_DIR`-redirected contexts can never mint a beacon; (2) sidecar-absent-under-beacon is explicitly specified as non-terminal `finalize-deferred` with a named STUB-GATE; (3) the residual bind-window exposure in (b) is stated honestly in the trust model instead of the current claim that pytest contexts "bind other ports."

findings.criterion: 3 — The latch cannot be burned hermetically
findings.section: Phase 2 — repair path for the 3 poisoned records
findings.message: The repair script is the ONLY primitive in the entire design that DELETES a claim file — the highest-blast-radius operation in the CAS namespace — yet its stated guards (hardcoded 3-id allowlist, current-state verification, refuse-second-run) omit the hermetic-marker refusal, the service-reachable probe, and the never-imported-by-suite conformance grep that the lower-blast-radius backfill tool gets. A claim deletion racing a live service (which could be mid-sweep on those very sessions once they're re-stamped deferred) or executed from a hermetic context should be structurally refused, not merely unlikely. Give the repair script the identical operator-CLI admission row in the trust-model table — it is a CAS writer (a negative one) and the table claims to be exhaustive over writers.

findings.criterion: 4 — honest per-session outcome list
findings.section: Phase 3 vocabulary / Phase 4 sweep / Phase 7 backfill outcomes
findings.message: `finalize-deferred` is retried by the widened sweep every ~30 minutes forever, and the closed vocabulary contains `unmeasured`, but no rule anywhere states WHO transitions a session from deferred to `unmeasured` or on what evidence. The backfill's outcome list reports "no-sidecar" but the plan does not say it writes a terminal state back; the Non-goals promise "honestly unmeasured FOREVER" for uncorrelatable sessions, yet as specified those sessions sit in `finalize-deferred` — a state the plan defines as retryable — accumulating perpetual sweep retries and a permanently-yellow healthcheck WARN that trains the eye to ignore it (the exact failure mode the locked severity rule exists to prevent). Specify the deferred→unmeasured transition: owner (backfill for historical; the sweep after live-sidecar-confirmed-absent-post-pruning for forward), evidence required, and a test.

findings.criterion: 2 — Interactive spend surfaces
findings.section: Phase 6 — surfaces / CLI mirror / coverage report
findings.message: The project's established convention is token-authed endpoints with 401-before-substance, and spend data (dollar estimates, model identities, per-lane usage distributions) is exactly the class of data that convention exists to protect on a Tailscale-exposable host. Phase 6 specifies rollup keys, render helpers, and a CLI mirror but never states the auth posture of any new or modified HTTP surface carrying spend data (the coverage report's healthcheck consumer, any JSON the project-window JS fetches for the new lines). Probably everything rides existing authed routes — but "probably" is not a spec on a security-relevant surface. One sentence pinning "all spend data rides existing token-authed routes; any new route is token-authed with the standard 401-before-substance test" closes it.

findings.criterion: 3 — regression-tested latch behavior
findings.section: Phase 3 — closed provenance vocabulary vs Phase 2 repair ordering
findings.message: The observed legacy value `sidecar-root-unavailable` is not in the frozen `usage_state` set, and the conformance test asserts no writer emits outside the set — but READERS (surfaces, coverage report) must still tolerate the legacy value in any window before the Phase-2 repair runs, and defensively forever (the repair could be deferred or partially fail). State explicitly that the vocabulary conformance binds writers only, and that readers render unknown/legacy states honestly (e.g. as their literal string), never crash or coerce to a known state.

The changelog ("Applied a search/replace patch" ×10, zero semantic content) confirms the reviser patched blind and never re-read the assembled artifact. This is not a formatting nit: the plan document IS the deliverable, and as written it is unshippable. Deduplicate, restore item 2 to one intact sentence, and diff the two copies to prove no divergent edits were stranded in the dead copy.
findings.message: The draft contains a complete second copy of itself embedded mid-sentence. Phase 4's launch-surface table item 2 reads "…envelope-measured today (real `# Master Plan (draft)" — and then the ENTIRE document (North Star, Phases 0–3) repeats, before the original sentence resumes hundreds of lines later with ", stays distinct per Stage-0 decision 3)". The content that got severed is precisely the

findings.section: all phase headings vs in-body references
findings.criterion: 4 — History recovered (backfill ordering references)
findings.message: Every heading carries two numbers ("Phase 7 — Phase 6 — Historical backfill") while every in-body cross-reference uses only the inner one ("the Phase 6 backfill tool", "the Phase-2-tested munging function", "the Phase-1 claim path"). "Phase 6" therefore names the Surfaces phase by heading and the Backfill phase by reference — in the same document. The backfill/snapshot contract (criterion 4) is held together entirely by these cross-references ("Phase 6 reads the Phase-0 archive… using the Phase-2 munging function"), so a maintainer or Stage-2 wave-mapper resolving them against the headings wires the wrong dependencies. Pick ONE numbering, renumber every heading and every reference, and add a criterion→phase map so the resolution is mechanical.

findings.topic: closed vocabulary omits the intake failure mode
findings.section: Phase 2 (CLOSED provenance vocabulary) vs Phase 1 repair path
findings.criterion: 3 — The latch cannot be burned hermetically
findings.message: The frozen `usage_state` vocabulary excludes `sidecar-root-unavailable` — yet that state demonstrably exists on disk (3 intake records), the Phase-1 repair script's precondition check must RECOGNIZE it ("verify the current state is still `sidecar-root-unavailable`"), and, worse, the plan never defines what a BEACONED finalize emits when the sidecar root or the session's sidecar file is missing at finalize time — the exact failure mode that caused the intake poisoning. Does it defer? Emit `unmeasured`? Consume the claim? The conformance test asserting "no writer ever emits a value outside these sets" will either fail against reality or force an ad-hoc, untested state back in — vocabulary drift by emergency, the precise accretion the freeze exists to prevent. Name the sidecar-missing-under-beacon outcome explicitly (it should be non-CAS-consuming and retryable), and state whether legacy out-of-vocabulary states are reader-tolerated or migrated.

findings.section: Phase 1 (hermetic beacon, CAS trust model)
findings.criterion: 3 — The latch cannot be burned hermetically
findings.message: The plan claims to "invert the hermetic predicate from blocklist to positive identity," but the beacon mint condition is "exclusive bind on 8777 + the REAL un-redirected data dir" — and determining "un-redirected" is itself a blocklist check over redirect seams (is `ANCHOR_DATA_DIR` set?). The foresight brief names a SECOND seam the beacon predicate never consults: `ANCHOR_SIDECAR_DIR`, "the only hermetic escape." A manual-debug run on 8777 with the real data dir but a redirected sidecar root mints a valid beacon, is admitted to the CAS, reads the wrong (empty) sidecar root, and consumes the claim — recreating the poison class criterion 3 exists to kill, through the front door of the trust model. Either the beacon mint must refuse when ANY redirect seam is active (and the plan must maintain that seam list as new seams are added — say so, so a future maintainer adding a seam knows to touch the beacon), or a beaconed finalize that cannot locate the sidecar must be non-CAS-consuming per Finding 3. The "no supervisor enumeration to get wrong" boast is overstated; it traded supervisor enumeration for seam enumeration and didn't write the seam list down.

findings.topic: eager skill-layer finalize structurally forbidden by own trust model
findings.section: Phase 3 (launch-surface table tier 5, deferred items) vs Phase 1 trust model
findings.criterion: 1 — Swarm spend visible going forward
findings.message: Stage-0 decision 4 locks "BOTH eager owner finalize + reconcile-dead catch-all." But under the Phase-1 trust model, only the beaconed server process may consume the CAS — and the agy-dispatch orchestrator is a separate CLI process that can never hold the beacon. The plan's own deferred item ("eager IN-PROCESS finalize inside the agy-dispatch skill itself") is therefore structurally impossible as named: a future maintainer who picks up that deferred task will build it, watch the beacon refuse admission on every call, and have to invent an unplanned workaround (a service finalize endpoint? beacon delegation?) at the highest-risk primitive. For the entire skill-layer swarm — 106 of 111 registry sessions, the population criterion 1 exists for — "eager owner finalize" quietly degrades to "sweep-only, up to ~30 minutes late," which is fine but is a MATERIAL narrowing of a locked decision that the plan should state honestly rather than defer as if it were buildable. Either specify the mechanism (e.g. the orchestrator POSTs a finalize request to the beaconed service, which performs the admitted write) or amend the deferred item to say sweep-is-the-owner for skill-layer sessions, permanently.

findings.section: Phase 1 (deferred stamping) + Phase 3 (widened sweep)
findings.criterion: 3 — a later live finalize can still measure (and 6, honest counting)
findings.message: `finalize-deferred` is retryable forever: the ~30-minute sweep "RETR[ies] every finalize-deferred record" with no exit condition, and the healthcheck WARNs "when live-registry sessions accumulate deferrals." A session whose sidecar never existed (or was pruned pre-capture) will defer on every sweep until the end of time — the deferred count only grows, and the yellow WARN becomes permanent wallpaper. The plan itself pins the locked severity rule's rationale: "a false alarm just trains the eye to ignore the banner." A permanently-yellow WARN is the same hazard one tier down. The vocabulary contains `unmeasured` but no transition rule deferred→unmeasured is defined anywhere — a future maintainer inherits an unbounded retry queue with no policy for declaring a session honestly unmeasurable. Define the terminality rule (e.g. N sweeps or sidecar-provably-absent ⇒ `unmeasured`, terminal, non-CAS-consuming... or explicitly "deferred is forever, WARN only above a delta threshold") — either is defensible; silence is not.

findings.section: Phase 3 (forward orphan-sidecar sweep)
findings.criterion: 1 — Swarm spend visible going forward
findings.message: The sweep's stated trigger is "sidecars whose DIRNAME embeds a valid session marker but has no registry row" — but the dirname is keyed to a CWD, and the sweep's explicit target population (tier-b skill-layer spawns that bypass the wrapper, i.e. a skill invoking raw `claude` from inside a parent session's worktree) produces exactly the collision case: MULTIPLE session JSONL files inside ONE dirname that embeds the PARENT's session id. Does the sweep mint one record per dir (silently summing sub-agents into the parent)? One per JSONL file (against what session id — they have engine UUIDs, no registry rows)? Skip as ambiguous (silently dropping the very spend the tier-b catch-all promises to catch)? The plan specifies dirname↔id correlation for the ONE-file-per-dir case and says nothing about N-files-per-dir, which is the dominant bypass shape. Specify the attribution rule (parent-attribution with a `via-parent-worktree` provenance note would be honest) — otherwise "never invisible" is asserted, not designed.

findings.section: Phase 2 (quiesce check)
findings.criterion: 3 — The latch cannot be burned hermetically
findings.message: "Truncated tail → `usage_state: measured-partial`, never a clean-looking number" — but does writing a measured-partial record CONSUME the exclusive-create claim? If yes, a transiently-truncated sidecar (AV lock, partial flush that the N-second mtime window happened to miss) permanently latches an undercount that append-only forbids ever correcting — a burned-latch variant in miniature. If no, what stops every subsequent sweep from re-reading and re-emitting? The claim-file semantics are defined for measured/deferred but not for partial. One sentence fixes it (e.g. partial consumes the claim ONLY after quiesce confirms the file can no longer grow — process provably dead — else defer).

findings.topic: snapshot read-only protection ineffective on Windows
findings.section: Phase 0 (plan-time sidecar snapshot)
findings.criterion: 4 — History recovered, honestly labeled
findings.message: "Mark the archive read-only (attrib +R / ACL)" — on Windows, `attrib +R` on a DIRECTORY does not prevent creation, modification, or deletion of files within it; it is cosmetically meaningless for the stated goal. Only a deny-write ACL actually freezes the archive, and the plan offers the two as interchangeable ("attrib +R / ACL"). A future maintainer will take the cheap option and believe the snapshot is immutable when it isn't — undermining the "frozen snapshot" premise every backfill guarantee is anchored to. Also, "the disk cost is bounded" is asserted with no number: 55+ dirs of full JSONL transcripts for multi-million-token sessions plausibly runs to gigabytes; state the measured size before committing to copy-everything, or the Phase-0 operator discovers it mid-copy. Specify: deny-write ACL (not attrib), and record the actual byte total in the plan once measured.

findings.section: preamble (second "## Success criteria" list)
findings.criterion: all (document fidelity to the locked North Star)
findings.message: The draft embeds the North Star verbatim (correct) and then immediately restates a paraphrased six-bullet "Success criteria" list. Two renderings of the locked criteria in one artifact invite drift — the paraphrase already compresses nuance (e.g. criterion 1's "where wired" qualifier, load-bearing per Finding 5, is dropped from the bullet). Delete the paraphrase; the verbatim block is the only copy that should exist.

reviews.note: Contrarian Shark, pressing the steel-man-the-premise angle. The draft's architecture is largely sound and honestly reasoned — so I have pressed hardest where the premise's load-bearing guarantees ("never invisible," "no measurement without a beacon," "one owner of deferred retries") are stated as absolutes the mechanisms as written do not actually deliver. One structural defect gates everything else.

findings.section: Phase 4 — launch-surface table, item 2
findings.criterion: 1 contract. The duplicate body must be excised and item 2 restored verbatim before any other finding can even be verified against a clean text.
findings.message: The draft is textually corrupted: launch-surface table item 2 breaks off mid-sentence at "envelope-measured today (real `#" and splices in a COMPLETE second copy of the entire plan (North Star through Phase 3), after which the original sentence resumes with ", stays distinct per Stage-0 decision 3)". The reviser's changelog — ten blind search/replace patches — is consistent with a patch anchor matching inside its own replacement text. This is not cosmetic: the launch-surface table is the plan's explicit "nothing left for Stage 2 to enumerate" enumeration serving criterion 1, and its second row (job_runner one-shot lane jobs — the envelope-$ path that Stage-0 decision 3 keeps distinct) is now unreadable. A Foreman handoff of this document would carry a duplicated North Star and a mangled

findings.topic: orphan-sidecar sweep cannot see shared-cwd sub-agent spawns
findings.section: Phase 4 — tier (b) sweep catch-all / forward orphan-sidecar sweep
findings.criterion: 1 — Swarm spend visible going forward ("A new fleet run produces measured records for its sub-agent sessions")
findings.message: Steel-manning the premise: the plan's guarantee for the DOMINANT population (106 of 111 registry sessions are swarm) is "measured eagerly where wrapped, by sweep otherwise — never silently absent." The sweep's predicate is "sidecars whose dirname embeds a valid session marker but has no registry row." But a skill-layer sub-agent spawned WITHOUT the wrapper (the exact bypass tier (b) exists for) typically inherits the parent session's cwd — so its sidecar lands under the SAME munged project dirname as the parent. That dirname embeds the PARENT's session id, which DOES have a registry row, so the orphan predicate structurally never fires; the sub-agent's spend is either silently folded into (or mis-attributed against) the parent, or never minted at all. The "never invisible" claim is therefore false for precisely the population criterion 1 exists for, and the enforcement backstop (a grep conformance test over Anchor product code) cannot reach the actual spawner either — agy-dispatch is a skill in a different repo whose runtime `claude` invocations are model-driven prompts, not greppable Anchor call sites. The plan must either (a) require per-spawn distinct cwd/worktree so the dirname correlation holds per sub-agent, (b) correlate at sidecar-FILE granularity (per-file session UUID) rather than per-dir, or (c) honestly demote the tier-(b) guarantee from "never invisible" to "invisible unless wrapped" and make wrapper adoption a gating deliverable, not a named task.

findings.topic: CAS trust-model invariant contradicts its own writer table
findings.section: Phase 2 — CAS trust model, writers 2 and 5
findings.criterion: 3 — The latch cannot be burned hermetically
findings.message: Writer 5 declares the invariant "No measurement without a beacon, ever." Writer 2 (the backfill tool) holds no beacon — it runs precisely when the service is UNREACHABLE — yet mints `measured-backfill` records through "the identical claim path." Both statements cannot be true. As written, either the invariant is false (and the trust model's headline guarantee is rhetorical, not real), or backfill needs a beacon it structurally cannot have. The fix is a restatement, not a redesign — the true invariant is "no CAS consumption except by the current beacon holder OR the audited standalone operator CLI under its own admission predicate" — but a trust model whose single authoritative table contains a self-contradiction has not earned the word "authoritative," and the STUB-GATE tests pinning criterion 3 will pin whichever reading the implementer happens to choose.

findings.topic: two competing owners of deferred-retry measurement
findings.section: Phase 2 repair path / Phase 4 sweep scope / Phase 7 target set
findings.criterion: 4 — History recovered, honestly labeled
findings.message: Phase 4 names the beaconed sweep "the single named owner of deferred retries," retrying every `finalize-deferred` record against the LIVE sidecar root on a ~30-minute cadence from the interim deploy checkpoint onward. Phase 2's repair path re-stamps the 3 poisoned records `finalize-deferred` and then asserts "the Phase 6 backfill measures them through the normal claim path." Both cannot own them: the sweep will reach those records phases earlier than backfill, reading the live root (which engine retention may have pruned differently than the Phase-0 snapshot), and whichever writer wins the exclusive-create claim forecloses the other. Consequences the plan does not resolve: (a) the repaired sessions may be stamped `measured` (sweep) rather than `measured-backfill` (backfill), so the Phase 7 outcome list's target set ("69 + 37 + 3 repaired-deferred") will not reconcile as written; (b) if the live sidecar was pruned but the snapshot copy survives, the sweep's retry fails first and the plan does not state whether a failed live retry leaves the record retryable for backfill or stamps a terminal-looking state. Name ONE owner per record class (e.g. sweep owns post-deploy deferrals; backfill exclusively owns pre-snapshot historical sessions, sweep skips them) or the "single named owner" claim is decorative.

findings.section: Phase 6 — synthetic-session predicate
findings.criterion: 2 — `__doctor__` is excluded from every surface
findings.message: The convention test "registering synthetic without the flag fails loudly" is unenforceable as specified: to detect that an unflagged registration is synthetic, the test must identify syntheticness by some signal other than the flag — which is name-sniffing, the exact mechanism the plan bans ("marker convention, never name-sniffing"). Either the test quietly reintroduces name-sniffing (acceptable ONLY inside the test as a tripwire, which the plan should say explicitly), or the guarantee degrades to "callers that remember the flag are excluded," which is a convention, not an enforcement — and per the project's own engine-vs-convention honesty table, it should be labeled as such. Also unstated: the migration step for EXISTING `__doctor__` registry rows that predate the flag; without it, criterion 2's "excluded from every surface" fails on day one for historical doctor sessions.

findings.topic: most-motivating deliverable sequenced last without a de-risking dry-run
findings.section: Phase ordering rationale / Phase 7
findings.criterion: 4 — History recovered, honestly labeled
findings.message: Steel-manning the ordering premise: "backfill LAST because the substrate must soak" was compelling when delay risked data loss — but Phase 0's plan-time frozen snapshot removes that risk entirely, and the claim path backfill reuses is soaked by every earlier phase regardless of when backfill's CORRELATION logic first runs. The intake motivation (106 unmeasured swarm sessions) is the single most user-visible deliverable, and it now lands in the second-to-last phase with zero earlier evidence that the correlation will actually recover a useful fraction. A read-only backfill DRY-RUN (correlate against the snapshot, print the recovered/no-sidecar/ambiguous-skipped outcome list, mint NOTHING) belongs in Phase 3 alongside the munging-function tests: it consumes no CAS, touches no record, and converts "we believe 55+ dirs correlate" from intake-time hope into measured plan-time fact — or reveals in week one that the recovery rate is poor while there is still budget to react.

findings.section: all phase headings
findings.message: Every heading carries two conflicting ordinals ("Phase 1 — Phase 0 — …", "Phase 2 — Phase 1 — …"), and the body text cross-references the INNER numbering ("Phase 6 backfill" meaning the heading labeled Phase 7). A Foreman wave parser or a human skimming headings will off-by-one these references. Collapse to one numbering scheme before handoff. (Out-of-scope per the inclusion test; noted at NIT only.)

reviews.note: Review pressed hardest through the security angle per the tasking. The draft's substance is strong in many places (the writer table, the closed vocabulary, the blast-radius bounding are genuinely good) — which is exactly why the remaining holes below matter: they sit at the trust boundaries the draft claims to have closed.

findings.section: Phase 4 — launch-surface table (row 2, job_runner)
findings.criterion: 1 — Swarm spend visible going forward
findings.message: The artifact under review is structurally corrupted. Launch-surface table row 2 breaks off mid-sentence at "envelope-measured today (real `" and the ENTIRE plan — North Star, all seven phases — is spliced in verbatim as a second copy, after which the text resumes with the orphaned fragment ", stays distinct per Stage-0 decision 3)". One of the ten opaque "Applied a search/replace patch" changelog entries misfired and pasted the whole document into the middle of a table row. Consequences: (a) the first copy's Phase 4 is truncated and the second copy's Phase 4 is missing its opening bullets, so no single coherent statement of the choke-point launch wave exists; (b) the deduplicated content diverges between copies in ways a Judge or Foreman cannot adjudicate; (c) the changelog itself ("Applied a search/replace patch" ×10) carries zero information, so no Shark can verify what the revision actually changed — the corruption proves that opacity has already caused real damage. The document must be de-duplicated and re-emitted with a substantive changelog before any content verdict on Phase 4 is meaningful.

findings.topic: full transcript archive inside the repo tree
findings.section: Phase 1 (Phase 0 — plan-time sidecar snapshot)
findings.criterion: 4 — History recovered, honestly labeled
findings.message: The snapshot copies "the ENTIRE engine sidecar root — every sidecar project dir, unfiltered" into `.anchor/sidecar-archive/` — that is a byte-for-byte copy of every Claude conversation transcript on the machine, for every project (not just Anchor's), including whatever proprietary/commercial content those sessions touched. It is placed INSIDE the git working tree of a repo that already tracks and commits `.anchor/**` state files, and the sole confidentiality control is one conditional line: "add it to `.gitignore` if not already excluded." A read-only ACL does not stop `git add -A`; a single missed gitignore turns the most sensitive data concentration on the host into a committed — and, given this repo's remote-push machinery, pushable — artifact. The over-inclusive-copy rationale (munging rule untested) does not require in-tree placement: the phase's own verification step already greps for the `…anchor-worktrees-<session_id>` marker, so the same marker could bound the copy, and in any case the archive can live OUTSIDE the repo tree (e.g. `%LOCALAPPDATA%\anchor\sidecar-archive` or a sibling dir) with its path recorded in the manifest. Require: archive location outside the working tree, OR marker-filtered copy plus a manifest listing of excluded dirs — plus a test asserting the archive path is never under the repo root.

findings.section: Phase 2 — hermetic beacon substrate / CAS trust model row 1
findings.criterion: 3 — The latch cannot be burned hermetically
findings.message: The plan specifies how the beacon is MINTED (exclusive 8777 bind + real data dir at startup) but never how it is PRESENTED at consume time. The residual-risk admission ("a malicious local process could copy the beacon file") reveals the implied design: the beacon is a FILE in the real data dir, and "presenting the matching beacon" means matching that file's content. That check is circular: any process that resolves the real data dir can read the beacon file and present it — and "hermetic context accidentally resolving the real data dir" is the EXACT bug class that caused the original poisoning (the healthcheck was not a telemetry test, so the Phase-2 telemetry-suite conformance test would not have caught it). As written, the positive-identity predicate degrades to "can read a file," which is anti-nothing. The fix is cheap and must be pinned: consume-time verification must be self-identity, not file-content matching — the finalizing code compares its OWN process identity (PID + in-memory boot token) against the minted beacon, i.e. finalize-with-consume is legal only in-process inside the beacon-holding server; out-of-process callers are structurally deferred. Add a named STUB-GATE: a process that can read the beacon file but is not the minting PID gets `finalize-deferred`, CAS intact.

findings.section: Phase 2 CAS design / Phase 4 sweep / Phase 7 backfill
findings.criterion: 4 — never overwrites a live-measured record; honest provenance
findings.message: The CAS convergence argument rests on "record content is idempotent (same session → same payload) so a double-fire converges." That holds only WITHIN a writer class. Across classes it is false: the Phase-4 sweep retries every `finalize-deferred` record against the LIVE sidecar root and mints `measured`, while the Phase-7 backfill targets the SAME historical population (69 no-usage-state + 37 uncorrelated + 3 repaired-deferred) against the FROZEN snapshot and mints `measured-backfill` — different provenance, and potentially different token totals wherever the live sidecar grew or was pruned after the plan-time snapshot. The interim deploy checkpoint at the end of Phase 4 guarantees this overlap window exists for weeks before backfill runs. Exactly one writer wins the exclusive-create, arbitrarily — so a given historical session's provenance AND numbers become race-dependent and non-reproducible, which is precisely the dishonesty class this effort exists to eliminate. The plan's race test pins only sweep-vs-eager (same payload); the sweep-vs-backfill pairing — the one with divergent payloads — is untested and unacknowledged. Require an explicit precedence rule (e.g. sweep/live-root measurement wins for any session whose live sidecar still exists; backfill claims only sessions the sweep has confirmed absent-from-live-root) plus a STUB-GATE for the divergent-payload pairing.

findings.topic: force contradicts the CAS trust model
findings.section: Phase 7 run discipline vs Phase 2 CAS trust model row 2
findings.criterion: 4 — History recovered, honestly labeled
findings.message: Phase 2's authoritative writer table admits the backfill tool on a fixed predicate that includes "service-unreachable probe (8777)" — no override is listed, and the table is presented as THE single trust model. Phase 7 then quietly adds "REFUSES to run while the service is reachable unless `--force`". That is an internal contradiction in the plan's own security spec, and the flag it introduces defeats the one guard that prevents the backfill from racing the live service's periodic sweep on the same claim namespace (amplifying Finding 4: with `--force`, the divergent-payload race is not an unlucky window but an operator-invitable steady state). The service-reachable refusal exists precisely because concurrent operation was judged unsafe; an escape hatch with no stated justification, no logging requirement, and no mention in the trust-model table is a hole, not a convenience. Either delete `--force`, or add it to the trust-model row with its admission conditions (why, when, what it logs, what additional check replaces the probe) and a test pinning its behavior.

findings.section: Phase 4 — forward orphan-sidecar sweep
findings.criterion: 1 — Swarm spend visible going forward (and the Statement's "nothing is ever fabricated")
findings.message: The forward sweep mints honest-provenance `measured-backfill` records for any sidecar dir "whose dirname embeds a valid session marker but has no registry row." Unlike the Phase-7 backfill — which cross-checks containment against the complete KNOWN-session-id set and demands exactly one match — the forward sweep's admission is stated as dirname-marker-plus-parseable-JSONL alone, with explicitly NO registry row required. That means the trust anchor for a spend record entering real surfaces is a directory NAME: any process (or accident — a restored/copied old worktree dir, a user hand-running `claude` inside a stale worktree path, a test escaping to the real sidecar root from the non-telemetry suite the conformance test doesn't cover) that produces a marker-shaped dirname with JSONL inside gets its numbers summed into the project rollup as measured spend for a session Anchor never launched. The Statement's "nothing is ever fabricated" is violated by construction — fabrication just has to arrive as a plausible dirname. Require the forward sweep to enforce the SAME exactly-one-known-session-id containment check as backfill (the "unregistered launch" case it exists for still passes, because the choke-point helper registers before exec — a sidecar with no resolvable registry session should be REPORTED as an anomaly, never silently minted).

findings.section: Phase 2 — hermetic predicate inversion
findings.criterion: 3 — The latch cannot be burned hermetically
findings.message: The beacon predicate is exclusive-8777-bind + real DATA dir — the sidecar root is not part of the identity. Two consequent holes. (a) A process holding a legitimate beacon but running with `ANCHOR_SIDECAR_DIR` redirected (the plan's own "only hermetic escape" seam) — e.g. a dev hand-runs the server on 8777, real data dir, with a leftover sidecar redirect in the shell env — is a fully-admitted CAS consumer that will find no sidecar for any real session. That is the ORIGINAL poison scenario (`sidecar-root-unavailable` consuming the latch) re-admitted through the front door, and the plan never states what usage_state a beaconed finalize records when the sidecar is absent — `sidecar-root-unavailable` is conspicuously NOT in the closed vocabulary, and no rule maps sidecar-absence to the non-terminal `finalize-deferred`. (b) Symmetrically, a pytest run while the service is stopped (e.g. mid-warm-restart) that spawns the real server module without redirecting the data dir wins the 8777 bind and mints a valid beacon — the manual-debug carve-out makes this by-design admissible, so criterion 3's guarantee silently narrows to "while the real service happens to be running." Require: (1) `ANCHOR_SIDECAR_DIR`-redirected contexts can never mint a beacon; (2) sidecar-absent-under-beacon is explicitly specified as non-terminal `finalize-deferred` with a named STUB-GATE; (3) the residual bind-window exposure in (b) is stated honestly in the trust model instead of the current claim that pytest contexts "bind other ports."

findings.topic: repair script under-guarded relative to backfill
findings.section: Phase 2 — repair path for the 3 poisoned records
findings.criterion: 3 — The latch cannot be burned hermetically
findings.message: The repair script is the ONLY primitive in the entire design that DELETES a claim file — the highest-blast-radius operation in the CAS namespace — yet its stated guards (hardcoded 3-id allowlist, current-state verification, refuse-second-run) omit the hermetic-marker refusal, the service-reachable probe, and the never-imported-by-suite conformance grep that the lower-blast-radius backfill tool gets. A claim deletion racing a live service (which could be mid-sweep on those very sessions once they're re-stamped deferred) or executed from a hermetic context should be structurally refused, not merely unlikely. Give the repair script the identical operator-CLI admission row in the trust-model table — it is a CAS writer (a negative one) and the table claims to be exhaustive over writers.

findings.topic: no terminal transition out of finalize-deferred
findings.section: Phase 3 vocabulary / Phase 4 sweep / Phase 7 backfill outcomes
findings.criterion: 4 — honest per-session outcome list
findings.message: `finalize-deferred` is retried by the widened sweep every ~30 minutes forever, and the closed vocabulary contains `unmeasured`, but no rule anywhere states WHO transitions a session from deferred to `unmeasured` or on what evidence. The backfill's outcome list reports "no-sidecar" but the plan does not say it writes a terminal state back; the Non-goals promise "honestly unmeasured FOREVER" for uncorrelatable sessions, yet as specified those sessions sit in `finalize-deferred` — a state the plan defines as retryable — accumulating perpetual sweep retries and a permanently-yellow healthcheck WARN that trains the eye to ignore it (the exact failure mode the locked severity rule exists to prevent). Specify the deferred→unmeasured transition: owner (backfill for historical; the sweep after live-sidecar-confirmed-absent-post-pruning for forward), evidence required, and a test.

findings.topic: auth posture of new spend surfaces unstated
findings.section: Phase 6 — surfaces / CLI mirror / coverage report
findings.criterion: 2 — Interactive spend surfaces
findings.message: The project's established convention is token-authed endpoints with 401-before-substance, and spend data (dollar estimates, model identities, per-lane usage distributions) is exactly the class of data that convention exists to protect on a Tailscale-exposable host. Phase 6 specifies rollup keys, render helpers, and a CLI mirror but never states the auth posture of any new or modified HTTP surface carrying spend data (the coverage report's healthcheck consumer, any JSON the project-window JS fetches for the new lines). Probably everything rides existing authed routes — but "probably" is not a spec on a security-relevant surface. One sentence pinning "all spend data rides existing token-authed routes; any new route is token-authed with the standard 401-before-substance test" closes it.

findings.section: Phase 3 — closed provenance vocabulary vs Phase 2 repair ordering
findings.criterion: 3 — regression-tested latch behavior
findings.message: The observed legacy value `sidecar-root-unavailable` is not in the frozen `usage_state` set, and the conformance test asserts no writer emits outside the set — but READERS (surfaces, coverage report) must still tolerate the legacy value in any window before the Phase-2 repair runs, and defensively forever (the repair could be deferred or partially fail). State explicitly that the vocabulary conformance binds writers only, and that readers render unknown/legacy states honestly (e.g. as their literal string), never crash or coerce to a known state.
